text:
Priya Shah: Quick sync: telemetry shows a spike of `schema_error` for requests hitting /v3 where `context.env` is a string. This started after yesterday's v3 canonical schema enforcement in canary. We need a short-term compat playbook so we don't break customers.

Tom Nguyen: Can you share an example failure?

Priya Shah: e.g. payload had `\"context\": { \"env\": \"staging\" }` but schema expects `env` to be an object like `{ name: 'staging', region: 'us-west' }`.

Eloise Gomez: That's predictable. Lots of older SDKs still send the shorthand. I propose we implement a three-stage approach: detect+log, shim+warn, then enforce.

Priya Shah: Outline?

Eloise Gomez: Stage A (detect-only, 72h): gateway accepts both shapes but increments `compat.v3.context_string_detected` per-tenant. No behavioral changes.

Tom Nguyen: Stage B (shim+warning, 7-14 days): runtime performs a non-invasive rewrite so server sees the object form (map string-> { name: value }) and we add a `Warning` response header and a `X-Compat-V3: context-string` header for SDKs. Also send a minimal anonymized sample payload to `support-compat` topic (scrubbed).

Priya Shah: How do you feel about scrubbing and sampling? We want useful artifacts but no PII.

Eloise Gomez: Use existing scrubber + 1% sampling for full payloads, and aggregate counts for the rest. Include tenant_id and region tags.

Tom Nguyen: For Dedicated/private installs we should not rewrite by default. Offer a console toggle `compat.v3.context_rewrite` per-tenant. Hosted customers get an opt-out model, not opt-in.

Priya Shah: Agreed. Also add a temporary HTTP request header `X-Redwood-Compat: accept-context-string` that tenants can set to opt their traffic into legacy acceptance without toggling flags. That helps partners while they patch.

Eloise Gomez: Edge cases: streaming responses where SDKs expect a different schema mid-stream, and batched payloads mixing old/new entries. We'll normalize per-item and attach per-item metrics. For streaming, emit a single `compat.v3.stream_context_mismatch` metric per stream and include the `X-Compat-V3` header upfront.

Tom Nguyen: We need to ensure the change is visible in Console: a new card showing top offending tenants, counts, and a suggested SDK patch link. Also include a one-click action to flip `compat.v3.context_rewrite` for that tenant.

Priya Shah: What about alerting? I want a paging rule only if a single tenant experiences >0.75% context-string rate over 6 hours and absolute > 1000 requests. Otherwise, notify SRE channel only.

Eloise Gomez: Sounds reasonable. Also create a short runbook step for rollback: if this shim causes regressions, flip the `compat.v3.context_rewrite` off at gateway layer to return to legacy acceptance without rewriting. Document steps to revoke the Warning header in that case.

Tom Nguyen: SDK guidance snippet for the JS/Go SDKs:
```
// JS shim for older apps
if (typeof req.context?.env === 'string') {
  req.context.env = { name: req.context.env };
}
```
And for Go:
```
if envStr, ok := req.Context.Env.(string); ok {
  req.Context.Env = map[string]string{"name": envStr}
}
```

Priya Shah: Implementation owners?

Tom Nguyen: Gateway/edge team: detect header, pass `compat-info` metadata, and support `X-Redwood-Compat` on incoming requests. (ETA: canary in 24h)

Eloise Gomez: Runtime: per-request normalization, metric emission, sample scrubber hook, and add feature flag gate. (ETA: 48h)

Victor Zhou: Console/Salesforce: surface offending tenants, one-click opt, and add migration messaging in tenant UI + email template for high-impact customers. (ETA: 72h)

Priya Shah: OK. Timeline: canary gateway tomorrow, collect 48-72h detect metrics, then enable shim+warning for hosted customers. Dedicated/private customers will be notified with suggested timeline and can opt-in via Console.

Tom Nguyen: One more thing: telemetry naming and cardinality. Use low-cardinality tags: `tenant_id`, `region`, `api_key_hash`. Avoid including free-form strings from payload besides sampled scrubbed body.

Eloise Gomez: Also bump retention for these compat metrics to 90 days so product/releng can analyze rollout velocity.

Priya Shah: Great. I'll write the short runbook and post to #eng-oncall and #eng-infra. Victor, can you prepare the tenant-facing migration note?

Victor Zhou: Yep. I'll include example requests, the Warning header text, and an ETA matrix.

sre-bot: Canary deployment started: gateway/compat-acceptance -> cluster us-east-1. Monitoring will report to #infra-deploys.

Priya Shah: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the initial canary window to decide the exact enforce date. :white_check_mark:
